artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a symplectic manifold equipped with a completely integrable Hamiltonian system, i.e. a smooth map $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ whose components Poisson-commute and are functionally independent on a dense open subset. A fiber $F^{-1}(c)$ is called singular if some $df_i$ fail to be linearly independent on it; a singular fiber is called degenerate when it is not modelled on the standard non-degenerate (elliptic, hyperbolic, focus-focus) building blocks of Williamson type.

(a) Investigate the topology and local geometry of degenerate singular fibers of completely integrable Hamiltonian systems and of small saturated neighbourhoods of such fibers. In particular, prove or disprove the following conjecture: for a generic / "most" completely integrable systems arising in the literature (such as bending flows on moduli spaces of $3$-dimensional polygons, the integrable system on the Grassmannian of $2$-planes, and the Gelfand–Cetlin system on coadjoint orbits of $U(n)$), every degenerate singular fiber is a smooth manifold or orbifold and is, moreover, an isotropic submanifold of $(M,\omega)$ — possibly even a Lagrangian submanifold when its dimension equals $n$. Develop the corresponding theory of symplectic invariants, symplectic normal forms, and stability under perturbation for these new classes of degenerate singularities.

(b) In the SYZ setting of mirror symmetry, let $\pi:X^{6}\to B^{3}$ be a Lagrangian torus fibration of a Calabi–Yau $3$-fold. Generic singularities of $\pi$ form $1$-dimensional strata of focus-focus type, but at finitely many isolated points of $B$ several such strata meet, producing special "intersection" singular fibers. Describe the topology, symplectic local model, and invariants of these special degenerate singular fibers occurring at intersections of focus-focus strata.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been confirmed in several specific examples since being posed: Bouloc handled the bending flows on 3D polygon spaces and the Grassmannian Gr(2,n) system; Bouloc–Miranda–Zung and Cho–Kim–Oh studied the Gelfand–Cetlin system on u(n)*, showing the singular fibers are smooth isotropic submanifolds (with Lagrangian "diamond" fibers); Cho–Kim handled the SO(n)-type Gelfand–Cetlin systems. The general conjecture for arbitrary integrable systems, the symplectic invariants/normal forms/stability theory of these degenerate fibers, and the description of the special intersection fibers in SYZ Calabi–Yau 3-fold fibrations remain open.

status_evidence.title: Singular fibers of the Gelfand–Cetlin system on u(n)*
status_evidence.snippet: Singular fibers are smooth isotropic submanifolds diffeomorphic to two-stage quotients of compact Lie groups; diamond singularities yield Lagrangian fibers.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the isotropic/Lagrangian nature of degenerate Gelfand–Cetlin fibers for u(n)*.

status_evidence.title: Lagrangian fibers of Gelfand-Cetlin systems
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm to detect Lagrangian fibers from the ladder diagram; relates degenerate fibers to vanishing cycles in toric degenerations.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a partial answer for Gelfand–Cetlin systems and motivates a general toric-degeneration conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Lagrangian fibers of Gelfand–Cetlin systems of SO(n)-type
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the analysis of singular Lagrangian fibers to Gelfand–Cetlin systems for SO(n).
status_evidence.claim: Further partial confirmation of the conjecture in another family of examples.
